items.title: 暧昧期最累的不是没答案
items.hook: 你在替对方补全剧情，才会越来越累。
items.body: 先把猜测放下：看互动节奏、回应稳定性和自己的边界感，不做读心或复合承诺。
items.cta: 先做一次私密关系解读
items.notes: Manual publishing only; no mind-reading claim

items.title: 想主动联系前先问自己一个问题
items.hook: 我是想表达，还是想用回复缓解焦虑？
items.body: 检查动机、时机和边界；表达可以清楚，但不必把自己放进追逐里。
items.notes: Manual publishing only; no pressure tactic

items.title: 冷淡不是判决，是需要观察的信号
items.hook: 不要用一条消息判断整段关系。
items.body: 看冷淡出现的频率、上下文和冲突后的修复，不立刻下结论。
items.notes: Manual publishing only; no guaranteed interpretation

items.title: 你不是想太多，你是在找稳定感
items.hook: 真正消耗你的可能是不确定本身。
items.body: 把反复猜测重新框定为稳定感需求，解读是镜子，不是命令。
items.notes: Manual publishing only; no diagnosis

items.title: 关系值不值得继续，看你有没有越来越像自己
items.hook: 喜欢之外，也要看你是否还能诚实表达。
items.body: 温和复盘继续、暂停或重新表达的信号，不替用户做决定。
items.cta: 得到一个更稳的下一步
items.notes: Manual publishing only; does not decide for user

items.title: The chat reread loop
items.hook: If one chat decides your mood, zoom out first.
items.body: 15 second script: phone face down, breath, then relationship map; frame Tianji Love as a private mirror, not certainty.
items.notes: Manual publishing only; no certainty claim

items.title: Before you react
items.hook: Do not let one cold sentence choose your whole next move.
items.body: 20 second script: pause, write the fact, write the story, then separate them.
items.notes: Manual publishing only; no pressure tactic

items.title: Look for repair
items.hook: Coldness matters most when repair never follows.
items.body: 15 second script: contrast one tired day with repeated avoidance; suggest pattern review.
items.notes: Manual publishing only; no mind-reading claim

items.title: The mood swing trap
items.hook: If their tone controls your day, zoom out.
items.body: 20 second script: notification, mood drop, journal prompt: what changed and what stayed?
items.notes: Manual publishing only; no diagnosis

items.title: Context before conclusion
items.hook: Cold does not always mean done. Warm does not always mean safe.
items.body: 15 second script: both extremes can mislead; choose a calmer question.
items.notes: Manual publishing only; no guaranteed answer

items.title: A cold reply is data
items.hook: A cold reply is data, not a verdict.
items.body: Short post: Look at frequency, timing, context, and repair. One sentence cannot carry the whole relationship.
items.notes: Manual publishing only; no perfect accuracy claim

items.title: Separate fact from story
items.hook: Fact: the reply was short. Story: they do not care. Do not merge them too quickly.
items.body: Short post: Clarity starts when you stop treating interpretation as evidence.
items.notes: Manual publishing only; no fake metric

items.title: Repair is the signal
items.hook: The real signal is often not coldness. It is whether repair happens after it.
items.body: Short post: Watch how the relationship returns to safety after tension.
items.notes: Manual publishing only; no outcome guarantee

items.title: Your nervous system is not a dashboard
items.hook: A tone shift can trigger you, but it does not have to direct you.
items.body: Short post: Use the trigger as a cue to pause and ask a cleaner question.
items.notes: Manual publishing only; no diagnosis

items.title: Do not chase the weather
items.hook: Do not chase every weather change in someone else’s tone.
items.body: Short post: You need pattern-level clarity, not minute-by-minute monitoring.
items.notes: Manual publishing only; no manipulation tactic

items.title: Why did they suddenly become cold?
items.hook: Start with context before conclusion.
items.body: Answer draft: Suggest checking workload, conflict, prior consistency, and repair behavior. Avoid claiming to know intent. Disclose Tianji Love if linking.
items.notes: Manual posting only; disclose affiliation if used

items.title: Does a short reply mean they lost interest?
items.hook: A short reply alone usually cannot prove that.
items.body: Answer draft: Encourage separating facts from interpretation and looking for a repeated pattern. Disclose affiliation if linking.
items.notes: Manual posting only; no certainty claim

items.title: How should I respond to cold texting?
items.hook: Respond from your boundary, not your panic.
items.body: Answer draft: Offer a neutral check-in template and a no-pressure pause option. Keep tone supportive and non-clinical. Disclose affiliation if linking.
items.notes: Manual posting only; no therapeutic claim

items.title: Creator feedback request - cold reply framing
items.hook: Would “cold reply is data, not verdict” feel safe for your audience?
items.body: DM draft: Hi, we are testing Tianji Love, a private relationship reflection tool. We are not asking for endorsement or posting; only feedback on whether this framing avoids fear-selling.
items.notes: Manual DM only; critique request, not endorsement
